name: Raw claim lines violate the business key (planted duplicate extract)
detail: A re-driven extract loaded one day of claim lines twice. These rows carry DISTINCT surrogate keys.

name: Surrogate key claim_line_key is unique even on the raw file
detail: Proof that a primary-key uniqueness test would have PASSED while the business key was violated. Test business keys.

name: Mart claim lines are unique on the business key after de-duplication
Member-month is unique on (member_id, year_month)
detail: The only sanctioned PMPM denominator. One row per member-month.

name: Type-2 provider dimension has exactly one current row per provider
Type-2 provider spans do not overlap
Claim lines with a servicing provider absent from credentialing
detail: An inner join to the provider dimension would silently delete these lines and the dollars on them.

name: Claim lines resolving to the -1 Unknown member
detail: Unmatched keys resolve to -1 so the mart stays joinable.

name: Claims with no Northlake encounter (care delivered elsewhere)
detail: By design. Northlake cannot see care it did not deliver, which is precisely why the hub is necessary.

name: EHR encounters whose patient never resolved to a member
detail: The EHR-to-claims join is a three-hop through the crosswalk and it loses this share. The loss is NOT random.

name: allowed = paid + deductible + copay + coinsurance + cob on every line
detail: Holds to the penny on 100% of lines, every adjudication version.

name: billed >= allowed on every line
Header total paid = SUM(line paid) per (claim, adjudication version)
detail: 388,869 claim-versions compared.

name: Both sanctioned nettings agree: all rows vs is_current_version
detail: Note there is NO reversal exclusion in the second formula. Orphan reversals are current and negative on purpose, so excluding them breaks the tie.

name: Naive span-sum overstates member-months versus the de-duplicated union
detail: Summing span lengths double counts every overlap. The correct denominator is the gaps-and-islands union.

name: Allowed PMPM, COMMERCIAL
Admissions per 1000, COMMERCIAL
ED visits per 1000, COMMERCIAL
Allowed PMPM, MEDICARE_ADVANTAGE
Admissions per 1000, MEDICARE_ADVANTAGE
ED visits per 1000, MEDICARE_ADVANTAGE
Top 1% of members share of allowed
detail: The single most recognizable realism check a payer audience applies.

name: Top 5% of members share of allowed
Average length of stay, days
Median paid lag, days
Every chronic condition prevalence within tolerance of its benchmark
detail: Worst deviation: HYPO off by 0.14pp.

name: P(diabetes | hypertension), emergent from the shared risk term
Sex-inappropriate diagnoses at MEMBER grain
detail: Enforced by the generator. Must be zero.

name: Master persons resolving to more than one distinct person
detail: The over-match detector. Two distinct people share one master_person_id, so the identity carries two dates of birth and often two sexes. One query finds them, which is what makes this a satisfying teaching beat.

name: Of those, how many the one-line sex-mismatch query alone would find
detail: Sex mismatch is the cheapest detector but it only catches the mixed-sex pairs. Same-sex twins need the date-of-birth check, which is why the audit view tests both.

name: length_of_stay_days equals discharge minus admit exactly
No encounters after the source window
No elective ambulatory encounters on weekends
Every NPI deliberately FAILS its check digit
detail: A valid NPI resolves to a real clinician in the public NPPES registry, which synthetic data must never do. Validators will flag these, and that is intended.

name: Encounter-type source values with no crosswalk entry
detail: One clinic emits a value nobody mapped. It lands as UNKNOWN and gets filtered out as junk unless someone profiles distinct values BY SOURCE.

name: Share of ambulatory volume landing as UNKNOWN
One physical hospital carries two EHR department identifiers
detail: An EMR upgrade renumbered the site mid-2024. Without the crosswalk, volume by facility splits one hospital into two as a step change in the middle of the year.

name: Share of ORTHO-NR closures landing at day 30 after the rule
detail: A spike at a round number is a workflow rule, not clinical behavior.

name: Same measure at every other site
Referral confirmation rate is materially worse at ORTHO-NR
detail: Confirmation is measured against a real event - a claim or a completed appointment - not against the status field.

name: ORTHO-NR ranks best of 12 on EHR-apparent out-of-network rate
detail: The naive single-source answer. This is the number that gets a clinic group held up as the model to copy.

name: Excess cost of ORTHO-NR leaked episodes over the in-network equivalent
detail: The joined answer. Episodes that went out of network, priced against what the same care would have cost in network, attributed to the referring site. This is the figure the narrative quotes - NOT total out-of-network allowed, which sweeps in every outside claim in the book and answers nobody's question.

name: ORTHO-NR share of system-wide referral leakage excess
detail: One clinic group of twelve, and it carries this share of the excess. That concentration is the argument.

name: Excess cost routed to Summit Point after its contract terminated
detail: Its contract ended 2024-10-01. The EHR referral directory still reads PAR, 14 months stale. A governance failure with a price tag, and nobody made a bad clinical decision.

name: Share of leaked spend that is plausibly recapturable
detail: Tested against real drive times and against in-network surgical capability and block time. At this panel size capacity does NOT bind, so nearly all leaked volume is recapturable. That is the opposite of what the design expected, and it is what the data says.

name: Why the remainder is not recapturable
actual: geography 0.0%, capacity 0.0%; 758 leaked episodes vs 2,283 in-network case headroom
detail: Named so the number can be defended rather than asserted.

name: Service month 2025-10 is materially incomplete
detail: Claims absent from this extract are exactly the ones that had not adjudicated by the paid-through date of 2026-02-28 - the slowest-paying, not a random sample. Designed completeness 78%.

name: Service month 2025-11 is materially incomplete
detail: Claims absent from this extract are exactly the ones that had not adjudicated by the paid-through date of 2026-02-28 - the slowest-paying, not a random sample. Designed completeness 54%.

name: Service month 2025-12 is materially incomplete
detail: Claims absent from this extract are exactly the ones that had not adjudicated by the paid-through date of 2026-02-28 - the slowest-paying, not a random sample. Designed completeness 31%.

name: Completeness declines monotonically toward the edge of the window
detail: The signature of runout. A real utilization drop would not get progressively steeper the closer you get to the extract date.

name: dim_date flags exactly the incomplete months
detail: claims_runout_complete_flag is the guardrail: any service-date trend should filter on it rather than relying on the analyst remembering where the data stops.
